44680-jungle-and-stream-or-the-adventure.title: The Adventures Of Two Boys In Siam
44680-jungle-and-stream-or-the-adventure.creator: Geo. Manville Fenn
44680-jungle-and-stream-or-the-adventure.description: A book by Geo. Manville Fenn. "What, me go and meddle there! Look here, Master Harry, I'll go with you fishing, and wade into that sticky red mud if you want me to; or I'll go with you shooting or collecting, and get my eyes scratched out in the jungle, and risk being clawed by tigers, or stung by snakes, or squeedged flat by an elephant's neat little foot; but I'm not going to interfere with old Ng's pots and pans. Why, he'd put some poison in my vittles."

arxiv-2101-11292.title: Distributed Learning over Markovian Fading Channels for Stable Spectrum Access
arxiv-2101-11292.creator: Tomer Gafni, Kobi Cohen
arxiv-2101-11292.description: Abstract We consider the problem of multi-user spectrum access in wireless networks. The bandwidth is divided into K K orthogonal channels, and M M users aim to access the spectrum. Each user chooses a single channel for transmission at each time slot. The state of each channel is modeled by a restless unknown Markovian process.

arxiv-2103-15597.title: RobustNet: Improving Domain Generalization in Urban-Scene Segmentation via Instance Selective Whitening
arxiv-2103-15597.creator: Sungha Choi * {}^{\text{*}} 1, 3] Sanghun Jung * {}^{\text{*}} 2 Huiwon Yun 4 Joanne T. Kim 3 Seungryong Kim 3 Jaegul Choo 2 [1]LG AI Research 2 KAIST 3 Korea University 4 Sogang University
arxiv-2103-15597.description: Abstract Enhancing the generalization capability of deep neural networks to unseen domains is crucial for safety-critical applications in the real world such as autonomous driving. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel instance selective whitening loss to improve the robustness of the segmentation networks for unseen domains.

arxiv-2110-02896.title: Predicting the Popularity of Games on Steam
arxiv-2110-02896.creator: Andraž De Luisa, Jan Hartman, David Nabergoj, Samo Pahor, Marko Rus, Bozhidar Stevanoski, Jure Demšar, Erik Štrumbelj
arxiv-2110-02896.description: Abstract The video game industry has seen rapid growth over the last decade. Thousands of video games are released and played by millions of people every year, creating a large community of players. Steam is a leading gaming platform and social networking site, which allows its users to purchase and store games.

arxiv-2112-14677.title: Gravity duals for defect quivers in the Veneziano limit
arxiv-2112-14677.creator: Niko Jokela1 niko.jokela@helsinki.fi, José Manuel Penín, 2 jose.peninascariz@helsinki.fi, Konstantinos Christos S. Rigatos3 konstantinoschristos.rigatos@colorado.edu
arxiv-2112-14677.description: Abstract We construct gravity duals to supersymmetric gauge theories in the presence of unquenched flavor hypermultiplets in the fundamental representation of the gauge group living on the (1+1)-dimensional defect. This configuration is given by the intersection of two sets of D3-branes.

arxiv-2312-01462.title: Categorical Relations and Bipartite Entanglement in Tensor Cones for Toeplitz and Fejér-Riesz Operator Systems Thanks: Supported in part by the NSERC Discovery Grant program
arxiv-2312-01462.creator: Douglas Farenick
arxiv-2312-01462.description: Abstract . The present paper aims to understand separability and entanglement in tensor cones, in the sense of Namioka and Phelps [ 32 ] , that arise from the base cones of operator system tensor products [ 30 ] .

arxiv-2401-10513.title: SAGE-HB: Swift Adaptation and Generalization in Massive MIMO Hybrid Beamforming Thanks: The authors are with the Department of Electrical Engineering, Polytechnique Montreal, Montreal, QC H3T 1J4, Canada. Emails: {ali.hasanzadeh-karkan, hamed.hojatian, j-f.frigon, francois.leduc-primeau}@polymtl.ca.
arxiv-2401-10513.creator: Ali Hasanzadeh Karkan, Hamed Hojatian, Jean-François Frigon, and François Leduc-Primeau
arxiv-2401-10513.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL)-based solutions have emerged as promising candidates for beamforming in massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (mMIMO) systems. Nevertheless, it remains challenging to seamlessly adapt these solutions to practical deployment scenarios, typically necessitating extensive data for fine-tuning while grappling with domain adaptation and generalization issues.

arxiv-2501-09077.title: Assessing the dark matter content of two quasar host galaxies at z ∼ 6 z\sim 6 through gas kinematics
arxiv-2501-09077.creator: Qinyue Fei, John D. Silverman, Seiji Fujimoto, Ran Wang, Luis C. Ho, Manuela Bischetti, Stefano Carniani, Michele Ginolfi, Gareth C. Jones, Roberto Maiolino, Wiphu Rujopakarn, N. M. Förster Schreiber, Juan M. Espejo Salcedo, Lilian L. Lee

Jones, Roberto Maiolino, Wiphu Rujopakarn, N. M. Förster Schreiber, Juan M. Espejo Salcedo, Lilian L. Lee. We conduct a study of the gas kinematics of two quasar host galaxies at z ≳ 6 z\gtrsim 6 traced by the [C ii] emission line using ALMA.

arxiv-2502-03793.title: It’s All in The [MASK]: Simple Instruction-Tuning Enables BERT-like Masked Language Models As Generative Classifiers Journal: Natural Language Processing
arxiv-2502-03793.creator: Benjamin Clavié, Nathan Cooper, Benjamin Warner
arxiv-2502-03793.description: Abstract While encoder-only models such as BERT and ModernBERT are ubiquitous in real-world NLP applications, their conventional reliance on task-specific classification heads can limit their applicability compared to decoder-based large language models (LLMs). In this work, we introduce ModernBERT-Large-Instruct, a 0.4B-parameter encoder model that leverages its masked language modeling (MLM) head for generative classification.

arxiv-2508-20305.title: Directed and Undirected Vertex Connectivity Problems are Equivalent for Dense Graphs
arxiv-2508-20305.creator: Yonggang Jiang, Sagnik Mukhopadhyay, Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai
arxiv-2508-20305.description: Abstract Vertex connectivity and its variants are among the most fundamental problems in graph theory, with decades of extensive study and numerous algorithmic advances. The directed variants of vertex connectivity are usually solved by manually extending fast algorithms for undirected graphs, which has required considerable effort.

arxiv-2601-00965.title: Adapting Feature Attenuation to NLP
arxiv-2601-00965.creator: Tianshuo Yang, Ryan Rabinowitz, Terrance E. Boult, Jugal Kalita
arxiv-2601-00965.description: Abstract Transformer classifiers such as BERT deliver impressive closed - set accuracy, yet they remain brittle when confronted with inputs from unseen categories—a common scenario for deployed NLP systems. We investigate Open - Set Recognition (OSR) for text by porting the feature attenuation hypothesis from computer vision to transformers and by benchmarking it against state-of-the-art baselines.

pmc-10704750.title: Health professionals’ perceptions of planned home birth care within the Brazilian health system
pmc-10704750.creator: Jannaina Campos Beviláqua, Laena Costa dos Reis, Valdecyr Herdy Alves, Lucia Helena Garcia Penna, Silvio Éder Dias da Silva, Andressa Tavares Parente, Fabianne de Jesus Dias Sousa, Bianca Dargam Gomes Vieira, Audrey Vidal Pereira, Maura Eduarda Sousa Fernandes, Diego Pereira Rodrigues
pmc-10704750.description: BackgroundThe American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, in its opinion of the Committee on Midwifery Practice, points out that planned home birth is a woman's and family's right to experience, but also to choose and be informed about, their baby's place of birth.

pmc-11464752.title: Effects of Climate, Soil, Topography and Disturbance on Liana Prevalence
pmc-11464752.creator: Emma J Mackintosh, Catherine E Waite, Francis E Putz, Marion Pfeifer, Chengrong Chen, Zhongming Lan, Sophie Brennan, Andrew R Marshall
pmc-11464752.description: Lianas (woody vines and climbing monocots) are increasing in abundance in many tropical forests with uncertain consequences for forest functioning and recovery following disturbances. At a global scale, these increases are likely driven by disturbances and climate change. Yet, our understanding of the environmental variables that drive liana prevalence at regional scales is incomplete and geographically biased towards Latin America.

pmc-11561907.title: How reliance on Spanish-language social media predicts beliefs in false political narratives amongst Latinos
pmc-11561907.creator: Marisa Abrajano, Marianna Garcia, Aaron Pope, Robert Vidigal, Joshua A Tucker, Jonathan Nagler, Noshir Contractor
pmc-11561907.description: False political narratives are nearly inescapable on social media in the United States. They are a particularly acute problem for Latinos, and especially for those who rely on Spanish-language social media for news and information. Studies have shown that Latinos are vulnerable to misinformation because they rely more heavily on social media and messaging platforms than non-Hispanic whites.

pmc-12652385.title: Insights into the Biomarker Potential of Humanin and Mots-c Expression and Telomere Length in Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-12652385.creator: Francisco Rodríguez-Esparragón, Sara E Cazorla-Rivero, Eduardo Torrealba, Ángeles Cánovas-Molina, Ayose N González-Hernández, Ruth Martín-Alfaro, María P Afonso-Medina, María T Martínez de Saavedra-Álvarez, Carmen G Pérez-Santana, Carmen Bartolomé, Lidia Estupiñán, Jesús M González-Martín, Bernardin
pmc-12652385.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Humanin (HN) and MOTS-c are mitochondrial-derived peptides (MDPs) known for their neuroprotective and metabolic functions. Their circulating and tissue levels decline with age and in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This study aimed to evaluate whether blood and plasma gene expression and plasma protein levels of HN and MOTS-c are associated with AD markers, their role in the conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to AD, and their overall association with the disease.

pmc-13116657.title: The Molecular Landscape of CASTLE: A Rare Thymus-like Head and Neck Cancer
pmc-13116657.creator: William C. Cho, Allen C. S. Yu, Wah Cheuk, Aldrin K. Y. Yim, James C. H. Chow, John K. C. Chan, Ka M. Cheung
pmc-13116657.description: Carcinoma showing thymus-like differentiation (CASTLE) is a rare malignancy arising in the thyroid or neck, with an uncertain cellular origin that complicates both diagnosis and treatment. To better understand its molecular underpinnings and identify potential therapeutic avenues, we conducted integrated whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing on six CASTLE and six thymic carcinoma samples.

pmc-13425951.title: The impact of self-efficacy and sense of coherence on hand disability during the first year after distal radius fracture surgery—a prospective cohort study

pmc-13643984.title: Burden of cardiovascular diseases in breast cancer survivors: a 9-year retrospective cohort study based on regional medical data in Inner Mongolia China
pmc-13643984.creator: Qiaorui Wen, Yunjing Zhang, Liying Qiao, Meng Qi, Ying Yan, Weiwei Kang, Guozhen Liu, Mingyuan Wang, Siyan Zhan, Yunfeng Xi, Shengfeng Wang
pmc-13643984.description: BackgroundBreast cancer (BC) and cardiovascular diseases (CVD) shared many risk factors. Hitherto no studies revealing the burden of CVD and its subtypes in mainland Chinese BC patients exist. This study aimed to describe the incidence, prognosis and economic burden of CVD among BC survivors in Inner Mongolia.

pmc-13675365.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Surgical Feasibility and Outcomes Following Neoadjuvant Immune Checkpoint Inhibition in Resectable Stage III and IV Melanoma
pmc-13675365.creator: T. Read, G. Nair, G. Velli, M. David, G. Bayley, Wen Xu, A. Barbour, B. M. Smithers, V. Atkinson
pmc-13675365.description: BackgroundNeoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) has demonstrated high pathological response rates in resectable stage III melanoma and is increasingly used for selected patients with low-volume stage IV disease. However, the surgical and perioperative implications remain incompletely defined. A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed to evaluate oncologic, surgical, and immune-related outcomes following neoadjuvant ICI and curative-intent surgery.

pmc-13685726.title: Ceramides and the Defective Barrier in Atopic Dermatitis
pmc-13685726.creator: Philip W Wertz, Joachim W Fluhr
pmc-13685726.description: BackgroundAtopic dermatitis (AD) is a common remitting-relapsing inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions, xerosis, and pruritus. It is associated with a defective permeability barrier and increased susceptibility to Staphylococcus aureus colonization. It has been demonstrated that the abrogated epidermal barrier is related to a decreased mass of ceramides and long-chain fatty acids in the stratum corneum (SC).
